Doors to the City Council Chamber will open at 1:30 p.m. for Open Session. Please be mindful that

ALTERNATIVE METHODS
The City provides the following two alternative methods of viewing and listening to the City Council Meeting
convenience:

  ¡  On Spectrum Cable Channel 35 with audio and limited video. Please check with your cable provider

  ¡  Live online through Facebook Live, with audio and limited video,

The disruption in service of any alternative method does not preclude the City Council or other legislative body
from taking further action on an agenda item.

Submitting Comments Prior to Public Meeting: Members of the public may choose to submit comments
electronically for consideration by the City Council or other City Legislative Body by sending them to the City
Clerk/Secretary at athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To
ensure distribution to the members of the Legislative Body prior to consideration of the agenda, please submit
comments prior to 8:00 a.m. the day of the meeting, and in the body of the email, please identify the agenda
number or subject matter. Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments receiv

meeting. Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

Inglewood, California
  April 9, 2024

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  April 9, 2024, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the City
  Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority at the hour
  of 2:00 p.m.
  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary announced the
  presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman Butts, Council Members/Successor Agency
  Members/Housing Authority Members Gray, Padilla,
  Faulk; and
  Absent:  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing
  Authority Member Morales.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as follows:

  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Mark F. Weinberg  City Manager/ Executive Director*
  Derald Brenneman  Acting City Attorney/Acting General Counsel*
  Louis Atwell  Assistant City Manager/Public Works Director
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority.

180  PRESENTATION - THE CONSOLIDATED BOARD OF REALTISTS
  INCORPORATED. Mayor Butts read and presented a certificate to the members of the
  National Board of Realtists.

  Members of the National Board of Realists accepted the certificate.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present
  who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority on any item
  on the Agendas.

  There was no response.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Faulk, and seconded by Council
  Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Padilla that the demands
  presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated April 5, 2024, in
  the amount of $6,223,043.75, and dated March 28, 2024, in the amount of $6,087,714.61
  are hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority
  Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said registers that said demands are so
  approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Gray, Padilla, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member
  Morales.

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Faulk, and seconded by Council Member
  Padilla that the Minutes for the City Council Meeting held on January 30, 2024, be
  approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes:  None; and
  Absent: Council Member Morales.
 April 9, 2024

132  CLAIMS DENIED. Letters from the Office of the City Attorney recommending the
  following:
  A. Reject Claims pursuant to Government Code, Section 913:
  1. Johnnie Dennis for alleged wheel damage; pothole on February 20, 2024.
  2. Wallace Dixon for alleged personal injury; standing water at Hollywood Park near
  Stadium Drive on September 2, 2023.
  3. Ty Garnero for alleged tire and wheel damage; pothole on January 15, 2024.
  4. Christopher Jefferson for alleged wheel and tire damage; pothole on February 12,
  2024.
  5. Ruben McCain for alleged wheel and tires damage; pothole on February 4, 2024.
  6. Franklin Merritt for alleged tire damage; pothole on December 24, 2023.
  7. Maaz Qidwai for alleged personal injury; hit by vehicle in Lot J at Hollywood Park on
  August 19, 2023.
  8. Mark Richards for alleged personal injury; metal plate at Hollywood Park near
  Stadium Drive on August 12, 2023.
  9. Anthony and Denise Taylor for alleged property damage; tree roots on November 6,
  2023.

  It was moved by Council Member Faulk, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that the
  City Council does hereby reject claims listed as A-1 through A-9. The motion was carried
  by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Morales.

125  PAYMENT AUTHORIZED – HARRIS & ASSOCIATES. Staff report dated April 9,
  2024, was presented recommending that the Mayor and Council Members authorize the
  payment of outstanding invoices submitted by Harris & Associates for legal services
  rendered for conducting an employee-related investigation.

  It was moved by Council Member Faulk, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that the
  City Council does hereby authorize payment in the total amount of $13,095. The motion
  was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Morales.

126  RESOLUTION NO. 24-46 ADOPTED - AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2023-2024
  OPERATING BUDGET. Staff report dated April 9, 2024, was presented recommending
  that the Mayor and Council Members adopt a resolution amending the Fiscal Year 2023-
  2024 Operating Budget, in the amount of $462,015, to pay an outstanding invoice submitted
  by the Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder/County Clerk, for the November 8, 2022
  General Election.

  It was moved by Council Member Faulk, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  Resolution No. 24-46 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2023-
  2024 BUDGET TO APPROPRIATE $462,015.00 FOR THE CITY CLERK
  – ELECTIONS CONTRACT SERVICES – FUND

  be adopted. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Morales.

  2
 April 9, 2024

142  AGREEMENT NO. 24-175 APPROVED – GRUBER AND LOPEZ, INC.;
  RESOLUTION NO. 24-47 ADOPTED - AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2023-2024
  OPERATING BUDGET. Staff report dated April 9, 2024, was presented recommending
  that the Mayor and Council Members approve a three-year agreement with Gruber and

  the Mayor and Council Members approve Restricted Grant Agreement (RGA), CCL-

  Neighborhood Beautification Project.

  It was moved by Council Member Faulk, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that the
  City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Restricted Grant Agreement (RGA) No. 24-176; and
  2) Adopt Resolution No. 24-48 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,

  AGREEMENTS  WITH  THE  CALIFORNIA  DEPARTMENT  OF
  TRANSPORTATION FOR THE CLEAN CALIFORNIA LOCAL GRANT
  PROGRAM – INGLEWOOD NEIGHBORHOOD BEAUTIFICATION PROJECT

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes:  None; and
  Absent: Council Member Morales.

178  AGREEMENT NO. 24-177 APPROVED – LEVERAGE INFORMATION
  SYSTEMS, INC. (LEVERAGE); RESOLUTION NO. 24-49 ADOPTED -
  AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2023-2024 OPERATING BUDGET. Staff report
  dated April 9, 2024, was presented recommending that the Mayor and Council Members
  approve an agreement with Leverage Information Systems, Inc. (Leverage), for goods and
  services related to the expansion of the Police Department’s camera system.

  3
 April 9, 2024

  It was moved by Council Member Faulk, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that the
  City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Agreement No. 24-177 in the total amount of
  $93,084.31 (includes a ten percent (10%) contingency in the amount of $8,462.21); and 2)

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE 2023-2024 ANNUAL BUDGET

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;

183  RESOLUTION NO. 24-50 ADOPTED - SUMMARILY VACATING A PORTION OF
  102ND STREET, WEST OF DOTY AVENUE. Staff report dated April 9, 2024, was
  presented recommending that the Mayor and Council Members adopt a resolution to
  summarily vacate a portion of 102nd Street, west of Doty Avenue, and quitclaim any and all
  related roadway easement rights over the applicable property.

  It was moved by Council Member Faulk, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  Resolution No. 24-50 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, SUMMARILY VACATING A PORTION OF 102ND STREET
  WEST OF DOTY AVENUE CONSISTING OF ABOUT 48,950 SQUARE FEET
  BETWEEN [WEST CENTURY BOULEVARD AND WEST 104TH STREET,
  EAST OF SOUTH PRAIRIE AVENUE AND WEST OF DOTY AVENUE]
  PURSUANT TO STREETS & HIGHWAYS CODE SECTIONS 8334(A) AND
  8335 AND GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION 65402(A) AND AUTHORIZING
  THE CLERK OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD TO CAUSE A CERTIFIED
  COPY OF THIS RESOLUTION OF SUMMARY VACATION TO BE
  RECORDED WITHOUT ACKNOWLEDGMENT, CERTIFICATE OF
  ACKNOWLEDGMENT, OR FURTHER PROOF, IN THE OFFICE OF THE LOS
  ANGELES COUNTY RECORDER PER STREETS & HIGHWAYS CODE
  SECTION 8336 AND GOVERNMENT CODE SECTIONS 6103 AND 27383

  be adopted. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Morales.

  REPORTS – CITY MANAGER. City Manager Mark F. Weinberg reported on the
  retirement of former Parks and Recreation Director Sabrina Barnes. He stated that 35
  applicants applied throughout the state for the position through a rigorous competitive
  process. In addition, he noted that the panelists consisted of internal and external
  experts, and they narrowed the field down to three finalists. The City Manager
  announced the appointment of Thomas Uwal as the new Parks and Recreation Director.
  He mentioned that Thomas has 21 years of experience in Parks and Recreation and has worked
  for the City of Inglewood for 21 years.

126  REPORTS – CITY CLERK. City Clerk Aisha L. Thompson congratulated Thomas Uwal
  on his appointment as Parks and Recreation Director and said she looks forward to working
  with him. The City Clerk thanked Council Members Morales and Faulk for allowing her to
  attend the Kick It World Event with them on Saturday, April 6, 2024. She acknowledged
  Volume Studios and mentioned meeting Jayden Smith, son of Will Smith and Joe Moses.
  She also stated that it was a fantastic event and well attended. The City Clerk reiterated her
  thanks to Council Members Morales, Faulk, and Sharis, who were valuable assets to her
  attendance at the event. She mentioned that her office would participate in the Emergency
  Preparedness Event on Saturday from 10 am – 2 pm and thanked Dr. Crystal McGlover for
  putting this event on again this year.

  4
 April 9, 2024

  Additionally, she informed the women about the registration opening for the 3rd Annual
  Women Rock Empowerment Summit and provided the website to register. She also
  informed the residents that Inglewood residents would receive priority in registration and
  that there would be a waiting list for everyone else. Finally, she reiterated that registration
  is now open for the Women Rock Empowerment Summit. She advised women not to
  register until the last minute, especially after hearing the headliner's name.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who wished
  to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not elsewhere
  considered on the Agenda.

  Lyric Armstrong, President of the Consolidated Board of Realtors, thanked the City of
  Inglewood for housing 37% of black homeowners. She stated that the City outhouse black
  homeownership compared to Los Angeles, which was 25%. She also thanked the City for
  being intentional about increasing black homeownership. She offered the Consolidated
  Board of Realtors’ assistance to the Council to continue flourishing the City with black
  home ownership.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned, at the hour of 2:33 p.m.

  Approved this ____ day of ________, 2024.
